This creates a DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability despite enabling a security option (escapeParameterHtml) . 1. intlify 2. vue-i18n # Issue: escapeParameterHtml does not prevent DOM-based XSS via tag attributes like onerror High kazupon published GHSA-x8qp-wqqm-57ph Jul 16, 2025 ## Package @intlify/core (npm) ## Affected versions >= 9.0.0 ## Patched versions 9.14.5, 10.0.8, 11.1.10 @intlify/core-base (npm) >= 9.0.0 9.14.5, 10.0.8, 11.1.10 @intlify/vue-i18n-core (npm) >= 9.2.0 9.14.5, 10.0.8,11.1.10 petite-vue-i18n (npm) >= 10.0.0 10.0.8, 11.1.10 vue-i18n (npm) >= 9.0.0 9.14.5, 10.0.8, 11.1.10 ## Description ### Summary The escapeParameterHtml: true option in Vue I18n is designed to protect against HTML/script injection by escaping interpolated parameters. However, this setting fails to prevent execution of certain tag-based payloads, such as , if the interpolated value is inserted inside an HTML context using v-html. This may lead to a DOM-based XSS vulnerability, even when using escapeParameterHtml: true, if a translation string includes minor HTML and is rendered via v-html. When escapeParameterHtml: true is enabled, it correctly escapes common injection points. However, it does not sanitize entire attribute contexts, which can be used as XSS vectors via: ` ` ### PoC In your Vue I18n configuration: `const i18n = createI18n({ escapeParameterHtml: true, messages: { en: { vulnerable: 'Caution: ' } } }); ` Use this interpolated payload: `const payload = '';` Render the translation using v-html (even not using v-html): `

... Sometimes we receive vulnerability reports on how it’s possible to do cross-site scripting (XSS) in Vue templates. ... HTTP security vulnerabilities, such as cross-site request forgery (CSRF/XSRF) and cross-site script inclusion (XSSI), are primarily addressed on the backend, so aren’t a concern of Vue’s. Sometimes we receive vulnerability reports on how it’s possible to do cross-site scripting (XSS) in Vue templates. In general, we do not consider such cases to be actual vulnerabilities, because there’s no practical way to protect developers from the two scenarios that would allow XSS: 1. The developer is explicitly asking Vue to render user-provided, unsanitized content as Vue templates. This is inherently unsafe and there’s no way for Vue to know the origin. 2. The developer is mounting Vue to an entire HTML page which happens to contain server-rendered and user-provided content. This is fundamentally the same problem as #1, but sometimes devs may do it without realizing. This can lead to possible vulnerabilities where the attacker provides HTML which is safe as plain HTML but unsafe as a Vue template. The best practice is to never mount Vue on nodes that may contain server-rendered and user-provided content. ## (EN) Best Practices The general rule is that if you allow unsanitized, user-provided content to be executed (as either HTML, JavaScript, or even CSS), you might be opening yourself up to attacks. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- CVE-2026-118257: High Cross-site Scripting in vue-i18n | SynScan (https://synscan.net/vuln/cve-2026-118257) 【turn138002search6】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 6 days ago; Crawled: today; # CVE-2026-118257 — kazupon / vue-i18n Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') ... Browsers decode the character references and parse the value as a same-origin nested HTML document, allowing attacker-controlled parameters or translation content placed in srcdoc to execute script when applications enable escapeParameter and render translations as HTML through v-html. ... * GHSA: GHSA-83rm-6c8r-g728 # CVE-2026-118257 — kazupon / vue-i18n Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') Vue I18n is the internationalization plugin for Vue.js. From 11.1.10 until 11.4.14 and from 12.0.0-alpha.4 until 12.0.0-alpha.5, sanitizeTranslatedHtml() escapes markup and event-handler text inside an iframe srcdoc value but leaves the srcdoc attribute active. Browsers decode the character references and parse the value as a same-origin nested HTML document, allowing attacker-controlled parameters or translation content placed in srcdoc to execute script when applications enable escapeParameter and render translations as HTML through v-html. Versions 9.14.5 and 10.0.8 are also affected and are no longer supported, while i18n-t rendering is not affected. This issue is fixed in versions 11.4.14 and 12.0.0-alpha.5. * Published: Oct 28, 2026 * Updated: Nov 2, 2026 * CVE: CVE-2026-118257 * GHSA: GHSA-83rm-6c8r-g728 * Severity: High -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Vue I18n: escapeParameter does not prevent XSS through srcdoc in translation messages · CVE-2026-118257 · GitHub Advisory Database · GitHub (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-83rm-6c8r-g728) 【turn138002search7】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 3 weeks ago; Crawled: 3 days ago; When `escapeParameter` is enabled (`escapeParameterHtml` in the Legacy API), Vue I18n passes the translated string through `sanitizeTranslatedHtml()`. ... `sanitizeTranslatedHtml()` (`packages/shared/src/sanitize.ts` in v11.4.13) works on the final translated string: ... * GHSA-x8qp-wqqm-57ph (CVE-2025-53892): the fix that added `sanitizeTranslatedHtml()` ... #### Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') const i18n = createI18n({ legacy: false, locale: 'en', escapeParameter: true, messages: { en: { message: '' } } }) console.log(i18n.global.t('message')) // v11.4.13: The browser decodes the value and renders `x` as a separate document inside the `
